conventions.convention: The metric has signature (−,+,+,+); null and causal vectors exclude zero. In a future inertial basis, future timelike means v⁰>|v_spatial| and nonzero future causal means v⁰≥|v_spatial|.

Weak piecewise C¹ histories have a finite partition, C¹ open pieces, and finite future timelike one-sided difference-quotient tangents. Derivative limits at corners are not assumed; proper time uses finite two-ended improper Riemann integrals. Hypothesis (H) is the stronger continuous-extension special case.

Inertial parametrizations are affine with constant future timelike tangent. Endpoint-bound equality also permits regular strictly increasing non-affine parametrizations; future orientation remains a hypothesis.
SI length coordinates use x⁰=ct, c>0, and η(U,U)=−c². A passive boost has x′⁰=γ(x⁰−β·x_spatial), with β=v/c; the primed basis uses the inverse boost.

A wave covector is nonzero; future null refers to its metric-dual vector. Dimensionless phase has components k=(−ω/c,(ω/c)s), |s|=1, and observer angular frequency is −ck(n)=−k(U_o)>0; ν=ω/(2π) and λ=c/ν.
Transversality in x means β·s=0 and gives ω′=γω. Transversality in x′ means β·s=|β|² and gives ω′=ω/γ. A normalized boost axis and aberration angles require β≠0.

E_n(P)=−cη(P,n), q_n(P)=P+η(P,n)n, and m(P)=√(−η(P,P))/c for nonzero future causal P. Kinetic energy is defined for massive P as E_n(P)−m(P)c². The total may be an empty sum, but zero has no assigned system invariant mass; a future null total has M=0 and no rest frame.

Massive particle momentum uses constant m>0 and P=mU; massless momentum is a separate nonzero future null primitive. Collision lists are finite and nonempty. Conservation and apparatus readings are adopted premises; thresholds are necessary conditions, not assertions of realizability.
The proper-time derivative of a C¹ field is P′/τ′. The four-force identities require a C² worldline and constant positive mass; the variable-mass clause is separately η(P,F)=−mc² dm/dτ.

load_bearing.statement: For c>0 and a weak piecewise C¹ future timelike worldline x:[a,b]→A, a<b, from p to q, cΔτ(x)≤T=√(−η(q−p,q−p)). Equality holds exactly for x(s)=p+σ(s)(q−p), where σ:[a,b]→[0,1] is a continuous strictly increasing surjection, C¹ on finite open pieces, with positive interior derivatives and finite positive one-sided endpoint quotient derivatives. Histories leaving the straight segment give strict inequality; the straight history attains T.

For inertial charts x′=B(β)x+b, |β|<1, and a future null wave covector with data (varpi,s), varpi′=γ(1−β·s)varpi>0 and, for β≠0, s′=[s+((γ−1)/|β|²)(β·s)β−γβ]/[γ(1−β·s)], with |s′|=1. At β=0 the data are unchanged. The inverse transformation uses −β.

For nonzero future causal P and future unit timelike n, E_n(P)>0 and |q_n(P)|²=E_n(P)²/c²+η(P,P). Future null P satisfies E_n(P)=c|q_n(P)|; future timelike P satisfies E_n(P)²=m(P)²c⁴+c²|q_n(P)|². For P=mU, m>0, η(U,U)=−c², E_n=mc²γ, T_n=mc²(γ−1)≥0 and q_n=mγw, with T_n=0 iff U=cn.

For a mass-specified conserving causal on-shell collision datum with nonzero legs and timelike total Q of mass M, each side obeys M≥the sum of its massive-leg masses, with equality iff that side is massive-only and all its legs are at rest in the center-of-momentum frame. A null total forces all legs parallel and null. For two massive incoming legs, M²=m₁²+m₂²+2m₂E/c², yielding the stated necessary outgoing-mass thresholds. A single null incoming leg cannot conserve against an outgoing side containing a massive leg.

The future closed cone is closed under addition, and adding a future timelike vector to a vector of that cone gives a future timelike vector. For v,w in the cone, −η(v,w)≥0, with equality exactly when either is zero or both are positive proportional nonzero future null vectors. A nonempty finite sum of nonzero future causal vectors is nonzero future causal, and is timelike if any summand is timelike. Observer energy and spatial momentum are additive.

Under the adopted inertial-covariance, ideal-clock/light and ideal-plane-wave postulates, the same wave in boost-related inertial charts has ω′=γ(1−β·s)ω and the stated transformed unit direction. An ideal inertial observer of coordinate velocity w reads γ_w(1−w·s/c)ω. The theorem supplies the longitudinal factors, the distinct transverse factors γ and 1/γ, and the aberration law, with their zero-boost qualifications and exclusions.

For a C² future timelike worldline with inertial coordinate path (ct,r(t)), constant m>0, P=mU and F=dP/dτ, F=mA, η(P,F)=0, dE/dt=f·w and F=γ(f·w/c,f), where f=dp/dt. For a C¹ positive variable mass instead, η(P,F)=−mc² dm/dτ.

For future timelike v,w, put a=√(−η(v,v))>0 and b=√(−η(w,w))>0. Then −η(v,w)≥ab>0, with equality iff v,w are positive proportional. Nonproportional pairs give strict inequality. The same inequality and equality characterization hold for two past timelike vectors.

alerts.finding: The Given paragraph attributes “the particle premises and homogeneous dust reading of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]” to that postulate. The cited postulate supplies particle momentum, observer readings, collision balance and a stipulated-force equation; it supplies no homogeneous-dust reading and explicitly excludes continuum matter. The theorem states its homogeneous particle realization separately, so the concern is the attribution, not its energy-factor calculation.
